meta_description_en: Letters to the editor in Outlet #70: L.G. Baumann discusses his Oxo programs, large number handling, and Plus D sector allocation bitmaps, with reply from Brian Cavers.

M O R E   M A I L ! !

    June, 1993        Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 L.G. Baumann.........03    08

 Francis Miles........14    20

 M. Atkins............21    24

 Chris Benyon.........25    29

 Alan Rutherford......38    39

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From L.G. Baumann, SOUTH AFRICA

Dear R & B,

On 3 April 1992 I sent you two
programs which you acknowledged.

The first was "Oxo Play" (63
sectors  - a Noughts & Crosses
programme with a difference. It
could be set for random play,
for the computer to play
defensively or for the computer
to attack by setting traps.

The second, "Oxo Traps" (38 sec-
tors),was an exposition showing
all the "Traps"that could be set
and also had a board on which
anyone interested could enter Os
and Xs at will to plan strateg-
ies and see what happened.

A common Menu linked the two
programs.

I noticed that the disc for
March had a lot of spare space
on it - 48 free slots and 431
k-Bytes - and I would suggest,
now that the Spectrum has been
separated from the SAM, the
programs could well be inserted
as "Add-enders".

The programs are complete and
could just be copied as given to
you. I am sure this would add to
the interest of your mix of
items.

I would be pleased to hear your
comments.


Thank you again for an excellent
"publication" and thanks too to
your many contributors.I thought
Ettrick Thomson's solution in
your November 1992 issue to
Malcolm Goodman's puzzle about
variables was superb.


There have not been any solut-
ions published as yet to the
further puzzle - how to handle
large numbers. Francis Miles in
his excellent and most versatile
accounting program "BOOKKEEPER"
seems to have found a method. I
know that it can show a rolling
balance of at least 8 integers
and 2 decimals.


My own program, "Big Totals"
published by "Outlet" in July
1991 (No.47) handles 17 integers
and 2 decimals but, alas, can
only add.


There is a point which is puzzl-
ing me which perhaps you or some
other reader can clarify...


I understand that each Directory
half-sector on a Plus D disc
carries a Sector Allocation Bit
Map in Bytes 15 to 209 for that
particular file only. When
saving a file how does the plus
D know which are the next sect-
ors available for use?


Is there possibly a part of the
disc which we don't hear about
which holds the complete bit-map
and which is altered with each
Save and Erase? Or does the plus
D quickly read the whole Direct-
ory each time a Save or Erase is
made and build up a temporary
Map in memory somewhere?Or what?

           L.G.Baumann

Brian Cavers to L.G. Baumann

By coincidence we entered your
excellent OXO programs into the
ADDENDERS in last month's issue
before reading your letter! We
are sorry for the delay but this
is a good opportunity to remind
readers that contributions may
take from one or two months to
many months before publication.

There are several reasons: one
is that there is a queue of
other programs waiting, another
is trying to keep a balance of
different types in each issue,
another is difficulty in editing
(real or imagined) while yet
another problem is finding room
for particular programs.


Although there is often plenty
of room on the +D disc version
of OUTLET, many readers forget
that the programs have to fit on
the other versions too. The Opus
version is the critical maximum
(excluding ADDENDERS) at around
180K with the +3 next at 203K.

Another problem with your part-
icular programs was that it was
easy to link them together on
disc but how do we edit them for
the tape version?

Anyway, we finally decided to
leave them largely unedited
(except for our transfer lines
which are essential to move
between systems) and put OXO in
ADDENDERS.


With hindsight,we might have put
OXO in ADDENDERS months ago but
another complication was Chris
Oliver took over and preparing
OUTLET programs last year and it
has taken me months to find time
to sort through my records and
send him not only outstanding
contributions but also any info
relating thereto.

Another unconscious factor may
have been that although your OXO
program was a definite MUST for
publication because I felt it
was the definitive and ultimate
word on the subject,nevertheless
we have had at least two NOUGHTS
AND CROSSES programs before so
perhaps somehow it was felt to
lose a notch or two in priority.


I have gone into this general
problem of some (not all!) of
the possible reasons for delay
of publication of contributed
programs in some detail (but not
exhaustively!) because I think
it's important that all readers
have some idea of what goes on
behind the scenes.

I might add that a good queue of
programs is a very healthy sign
and when contributions start
going into the very next issue
is the time when we should all
start worrying!

I might further add that we keep
a meticulous record of all the
programs sent in and a backup of
each on a separate disc so don't
worry about being overlooked.

Having said that, I suppose it
doesn't pay for us to be too big
headed so if anyone IS wondering
when their masterpiece will get
published, by all means mention
it next time you write -we don't
mind pushing one forward a bit
if possible.

Now, in your query about the +D
bit map - you guessed right - it
IS a map that is created as it
is needed by adding together all
the bit maps of each program to
form one giant map. This is done
with the simple machine code
instruction OR as I am sure you
will know and is rapid enough
even for a full disc. I do a
similar routine in my CATLOADER
file copy routine.


I don't know exactly WHERE this
temporary map is constructed but
it will almost certainly be in
the +D and Disciple RAM so might
be tracked down with a test disc
with known used sectors and the
new PEEK @ program I've written
which should be appearing in
OUTLET in due course. Of course,
it may take some months because
there is a queue...

                          Brian

         Francis Miles
           "Windrush"
          Rabley Heath
             Welwyn
         Herts AL6 9UF

       Tel: (0438) 813406


Dear Ron and Brian,

I notice Malcolm Perry (OUTLET-
TER in OUTLET 69) is asking
about a +D version of the OCP
Editor/Assembler and Toolkit: I
think he means "and Test Tool",
because the OCP "Machine Code
Test Tool" is incorporated as
part of the Editor/Assembler,
but the "BASIC Toolkit" is a
separate program.


So far as I know I own the only
copy of the DISCiPLE/+D version
of EA:I got it from Bruce Gordon
(I think he made it himself) in
the very early days of DISCiPLE.
I don't believe it's ever been
distributed commercially.

I used it a good deal but it had
some faults, and eventually I
took the trouble to disassemble
it and rewrite it in my own way:
this I called EA2.

I then rewrote it again putting
all SAVE/LOADs/LPRINTs in BASIC;
this EA3 will run theoretically
with any disc/cartridge system
or printer and I added a few
enhancements here and there. (It
doesn't work in 128K. I'm fairly
sure it won't work on a +3.

I've been using EA3 myself for
some years now, but never got
round to completely debugging
it and so never tried to market
it. Incidentally, I've also
written a disassembler, which
reads machine code and turns it
into a source code file which
can be edited on EA3.

I did some work on an EA4, which
was intended for the 128K and
would use the RAM disc to speed
up assembly and perhaps allow
even bigger assemblies - EA3 can
assemble up to about 20K of
machine code but such assemblies
take 20 minutes or so. But I got
bogged down by trying to be a
bit too clever! and left it to
get on with other things.


At present I've gone back to EA3
and hope before very long to be
offering a debugged and saleable
version, perhaps using some of
the extra ideas developed for
EA4.

Has OUTLET ever done a review of
the various assembler programs
(and perhaps even disassemblers)
which are available? I've looked
at the ones published by you
from time to time but have never
been tempted away from the OCP
program, which I've been using
for almost ten years now in
various forms.


Now for some errors in the ROM
Index...


I've been doing some work on
cassette SAVE/LOADs and found a
fairly deep error in the timing
calculations in my ROM Index;
chiefly under LD EDGE 1 and LD
EDGE 2 but the ramifications ex-
tend to other entries which dis-
cuss the timing of tape working.

Partly this was due to a mis-
print in one of my reference
books! It shows the time for IN
A,(nn) as 11 ticks, but really
it's only 10. So, the timing of
the sampling loop in LD EDGE 1
is 58 ticks, not 59 (Logan and
O'Hara were right) and most of
the errors stem from this. But
also in all my calculations I
omitted to allow for the 17
ticks taken to call the subrout-
ine itself.

I suspect that only a small min-
ority of readers are at all in-
terested in these calculations
so I won't go into more detail
but if anyone wants a detailed
correction, please drop me a
line.

Yours sincerely,


FRANCIS G MILES

Brian Cavers to Francis Miles

Surprisingly I could only find
an OUTLET review for one
assembler - the LERM Z80 TOOLKIT
and this was reviewed TWICE -
once in Issue 29 and again in 30
(I might add that we welcome
separate reviews from different
people).

Perhaps it's not so surprising
though because one tends to rev-
iew new material and, of course,
there has been very little new
Spectrum utility software in
recent years. I think I have
heard the name "ASTRA" raved
about more than once as being
the ultimate Spectrum assembler
but I don't think we've had a
review.                 - Brian

From M. Atkins, LANCS.

Dear Ron & Brian,

Many thanks for dealing promptly
with my enquiry re:"the missing"
Outlet for March.

I have now received the edition
for April and find Brian
Birkett's printing problem to be
very similar to that which I
experienced when I first
subscribed to Outlet early last
year.

I too use a 24 pin printer (Star
LC24-200 which in Standard mode
emulates the functions of the
Epson LQ-860 and in IBM mode em-
ulates the IBM Proprinter X24E).


At first I could not get the
TABLOID option to work properly
on A4-sized paper. The printing
overran by 6 lines and this was
remedied by switching the
printer to IBM mode and using
the "continuous" option on
TABLOID even though single sheet
printing is carried out. (See
Outletters April & May, 1992)


The enclosed sheet shows samples
of TABLOID printing using IBM
mode and then using Standard
mode. The former prints 9 lines
per inch (line spacing of 24/216
inch) and fits quite easily onto
A4 sheets whilst the latter
prints at 7 lines per inch (line
spacing of 24/180 inch).


The control code for my printer
which sets line spacing to n/180
inch or n/216 inch is <ESC> "3"
n (27 51 n). The printer manual
states that this code sets the
line spacing to n/180 inch if in
Standard mode and to n/216 inch
if in IBM mode. If n = 24 then
the line spacing is as described
in the previous paragraph which
makes me suspect that this code
is used in the TABLOID program.

If Brian can switch his printer
to IBM mode this may be the
answer to his problems.

           M. Atkins

Brian Cavers to M. Atkins



Many thanks. I did come up with
a solution to Brian Birkett's
printing problem but your solut-
ion will probably give a better
printout. It's nice to get TWO
solutions to a problem!

                       - Brian

From Chris Benyon, EAST SUSSEX



Dear Editors,

Many thanks for your excellent
publication. As one of those who
for various reasons decided to
invest in a PC(Ambra Hurdla 326)
I have been very interested in
your thoughts on the subject.

The Ambra comes with Windows 3.1
Dos 5 which includes QBasic, a
Mouse and SVGA.My own reflection
would be that there must be a
market for simple programs of
the Spectrum type which could
yet make use of the greater mem-
ory of the PC.


I nearly went bananas in the
first few weeks trying to get
even the most simple tasks done
and even succeeded at one time
in dumping the whole operating
system,impossible on a Spectrum.


I think typical of the unnecess-
ary complications is the DRAW
command in QBasic. There is a
separate command for up, left,
down right etc as well as a
command for from one point to
the other.


I would certainly be interested
in a PC version of Outlet.



In the meantime, I have just ac-
quired a copy of the 48K version
of the Spectrum emulator. It is
a joy to use but since I have
worked with the +3 ever since it
came out and managed to transfer
99% of my programs either dir-
ectly or with Multiface +3, I
need to be able to transfer them
to the PC without involving tape
- hopefully via RS232.What cable
should I use?

I have been trying to find a PC
program that would do the same
as Powerprint II [does on the
Spectrum] which was produced by
Buttercraft Software. You can
either make up a poster with
many excellent effects, 3D,
shadowed, textured etc with many


excellent style patterns, or
load any other screen and edit
or just print it in strips up to
any size you want.

It would be great to use it on
the PC or to find a similar
program. Can anyone help or does
anyone know the whereabouts of
Buttercraft Software?

     With every good wish,

        Yours sincerely,


         Chris Benyon

Brian Cavers to Chris Benyon

Many thanks for your PC info.You
don't say if your machine is a
286, 386 or 486 but it doesn't
sound as if it could be less
than a 286. I'm beginning to
think almost nobody is still
using less than a 286.

I agree it is VERY frustrating
to switch to an alien BASIC
after using Spectrum BASIC. I
had already been through this
before with the ST and finally
gave up in disgust. I was there-
fore expecting difficulties when
I began with QUICK BASIC on the
PC. However, my previous exper-
ience "over-prepared" me and so
although there is exasperation
it is not too bad for me!

I find the following drives me
up the wall in QUICK BASIC...

All function parameters have to
be put in brackets even when a
single value. Since 99.9% of all
cases are single values, e.g.,
PEEK 32768, CHR$ 65, STR$ RND,
etc., Spectrum BASIC is clearly
superior in that it only demands
brackets for calculated values,
e.g., PEEK (N+3), CHR$(X*8*2).

VAL is extremely feeble in QB.It
does not return the value of a
string but merely the value of
the first digits it finds! For
example, VAL"1+2+3+4" returns
only 1 because it stops at the
first non-digit while VAL"(1+1)"
gives 0 because it stops at the
first bracket!

There is no 'PRINT AT' so it is
not possible to do...

PRINT AT 3,3;"MENU";AT 6,8;"ABC"
;AT 10,4;"ETC. ETC."

You have to use...

LOCATE 3,3 : PRINT "MENU"
LOCATE 6,8 : PRINT "ABC"
LOCATE 10,4: PRINT "ETC. ETC."

Nor is there a PRINT apostrophe
so you can't...

PRINT'''"ONE"'''"TWO"'''"THREE"

        :..but have to repeat
PRINT
PRINT
PRINT          ...over and over!


Use of the mouse is strange too!
There is a separate cursor you
can move rapidly to anywhere in
the listing,click and the normal
is placed there - a quick way to
move around. However,it tries to
be too clever and doesn't place
the text cursor right where the
mouse cursor is but jumps to a
nearby keyword or space between
data. In fact, I cannot work out
how it decides what to do! It is
annoying as it is easy to put
the mouse cursor right on the
spot you want to edit only to
find it jumps 6 characters away!
Furthermore,the word or data you
are on may auto-delete when you
start to type! I think this is
while it is highlighted so one
has to take care to cursor first
and the highlight disappears.

The mouse scroll bar too makes
no sense to me at all on wide
screens and it seems impossible
to guess where it will end up!

The brackets on the PC keyboard
are one to the right of where
they are on the Spectrum and SAM
keyboards,DELETE is out of range
many other keys are different.It
is difficult because I have to
keep using different computers
all day!

One other thing... In most modes
you cannot even PRINT text on a
different coloured 'PAPER' back-
ground but only on the main
screen colour! Also, the border,
although smaller than a Spectrum
remains black!!
.

There are other problems but,
having said all that, ALL comp-
uters have their oddities. The
way the 48K listing scrolls and
rolls on the Spectrum drives me
potty unless I have my TOPLIST
(OUTLET 17) installed!

Once one gets used to one system
then anything new and different
seems alien and awkward. I have
outlined frustrations in QBASIC
yet as one gets used to them I
can assure readers that there
are many exciting new features
and incredible speed. If you had
been having doubts about getting
a PC then I can assure you that
I am enjoying it tremendously.If
you like programming in BASIC, I
think you'll like it too.


Like you, I found that the DRAW
command seemed awkward. However,
a week or so later I needed to
create a text routine to give
different sizes and styles of
text which we could use in any
future OUTLET on headers,prompts
etc. DRAW turned out to be perf-
ect for this as any character
can be redrawn to any scale, in
any colour and even tilted to
give italics! It can also have a
border, be pattern-filled and a
3D shadowing!

Although my routine will not be
finished for some time, I hope
to put it in a future OUTLET PC.
I think it will probably meet
your needs for a text routine
similar to Buttercraft's!


Now to your emulator problem. I
assume this is the Lunter one?
You can get a null modem cable
to link your computers but if
you have a serial cable on your
PC and another on your +3 then a
cheaper way is to get a null
modem adaptor which links the
two.

HOWEVER, the problem is that you
need a program both at the +3
end AND on the PC to transfer
the software and as I understand
it there is nothing suitable at
present.

I would advise you to order the
new 128K version of the emulator
from BG SERVICES (see OUTBOARD)
and use tape transfer.


BG are planning to build a few
PC tape interfaces for those who
do not feel confident enough to
make one up themselves. If you
ask, perhaps you can place an
advance order.

If you then use +3 TAPER (OUTLET
69), it will automatically save
your selected +3 programs from
+3 disc to tape and thence to PC
(all this presupposes you have a
cassette recorder!).

The Lunter emulator has really
been geared up for +D disc as
the 3.5" format is standard.

                          Brian

From Alan Rutherford

Dear Ron,

Brian mentioned he might do a
few lessons on how to use the
+D. The manual is hopeless, as
it does not state how much spare
RAM and what the pokes do in
machine code (what happens to
the registers etc.).

May I say once again, THANKS for
all the help that has been given
to me by both of you and various
other members of OUTLET ovr the
years.

All the BEST to you and OUTLET

             Alan

Brian Cavers to Alan Rutherford

We have a couple of articles
coming along soon as either OUT-
CLASSES or DRIVECHATS on using
the +D. One is by Malcom Perry
about using the hook codes and
the other by me about opentype
files.

Browsing through the manual, I
began to wonder what other sub-
jects I could cover. SAVE, LOAD,
etc. could have been covered by
more and better examples but it
is hard to find any ommissions.

If anyone would like to specify
a particular part of using the
+D I'll be glad to clarify even
if mentioned in the manual.


The other approach might be for
me to just, as it were, write a
new manual in instalments with
loads of detail and examples to
make even though part would be
duplicating what is already in
the existing manuals of the +D
and Disciple.

What do others think?

                          Brian.

I did some work on an EA4, which was intended for the 128K and would use the RAM disc to speed up assembly and perhaps allow even bigger assemblies - EA3 can assemble up to about 20K of machine code but such assemblies take 20 minutes or so. But I got bogged down by trying to be a bit too clever! and left it to get on with other things.

At present I've gone back to EA3 and hope before very long to be offering a debugged and saleable version, perhaps using some of the extra ideas developed for EA4.

Has OUTLET ever done a review of the various assembler programs (and perhaps even disassemblers) which are available? I've looked at the ones published by you from time to time but have never been tempted away from the OCP program, which I've been using for almost ten years now in various forms.

Now for some errors in the ROM Index...

I've been doing some work on cassette SAVE/LOADs and found a fairly deep error in the timing calculations in my ROM Index; chiefly under LD EDGE 1 and LD EDGE 2 but the ramifications ex- tend to other entries which dis- cuss the timing of tape working.

Partly this was due to a mis- print in one of my reference books! It shows the time for IN A,(nn) as 11 ticks, but really it's only 10. So, the timing of the sampling loop in LD EDGE 1 is 58 ticks, not 59 (Logan and O'Hara were right) and most of the errors stem from this. But also in all my calculations I omitted to allow for the 17 ticks taken to call the subrout- ine itself.

I suspect that only a small min- ority of readers are at all in- terested in these calculations so I won't go into more detail but if anyone wants a detailed correction, please drop me a line.

Yours sincerely,

FRANCIS G MILES

Brian Cavers to Francis Miles

Surprisingly I could only find an OUTLET review for one assembler - the LERM Z80 TOOLKIT and this was reviewed TWICE - once in Issue 29 and again in 30 (I might add that we welcome separate reviews from different people).

Perhaps it's not so surprising though because one tends to rev- iew new material and, of course, there has been very little new Spectrum utility software in recent years. I think I have heard the name "ASTRA" raved about more than once as being the ultimate Spectrum assembler but I don't think we've had a review.                 - Brian

From M. Atkins, LANCS.

Dear Ron & Brian,

Many thanks for dealing promptly with my enquiry re:"the missing" Outlet for March.

I have now received the edition for April and find Brian Birkett's printing problem to be very similar to that which I experienced when I first subscribed to Outlet early last year.

I too use a 24 pin printer (Star LC24-200 which in Standard mode emulates the functions of the Epson LQ-860 and in IBM mode em- ulates the IBM Proprinter X24E).

From Chris Benyon, EAST SUSSEX

Dear Editors,

Many thanks for your excellent publication. As one of those who for various reasons decided to invest in a PC(Ambra Hurdla 326) I have been very interested in your thoughts on the subject.

The Ambra comes with Windows 3.1 Dos 5 which includes QBasic, a Mouse and SVGA.My own reflection would be that there must be a market for simple programs of the Spectrum type which could yet make use of the greater mem- ory of the PC.

I nearly went bananas in the first few weeks trying to get even the most simple tasks done and even succeeded at one time in dumping the whole operating system,impossible on a Spectrum.

I think typical of the unnecess- ary complications is the DRAW command in QBasic. There is a separate command for up, left, down right etc as well as a command for from one point to the other.

I would certainly be interested in a PC version of Outlet.

In the meantime, I have just ac- quired a copy of the 48K version of the Spectrum emulator. It is a joy to use but since I have worked with the +3 ever since it came out and managed to transfer 99% of my programs either dir- ectly or with Multiface +3, I need to be able to transfer them to the PC without involving tape - hopefully via RS232.What cable should I use?

I have been trying to find a PC program that would do the same as Powerprint II [does on the Spectrum] which was produced by Buttercraft Software. You can either make up a poster with many excellent effects, 3D, shadowed, textured etc with many

excellent style patterns, or load any other screen and edit or just print it in strips up to any size you want.

It would be great to use it on the PC or to find a similar program. Can anyone help or does anyone know the whereabouts of Buttercraft Software?

With every good wish,

Yours sincerely,

Chris Benyon

Brian Cavers to Chris Benyon

Many thanks for your PC info.You don't say if your machine is a 286, 386 or 486 but it doesn't sound as if it could be less than a 286. I'm beginning to think almost nobody is still using less than a 286.

I agree it is VERY frustrating to switch to an alien BASIC after using Spectrum BASIC. I had already been through this before with the ST and finally gave up in disgust. I was there- fore expecting difficulties when I began with QUICK BASIC on the PC. However, my previous exper- ience "over-prepared" me and so although there is exasperation it is not too bad for me!

I find the following drives me up the wall in QUICK BASIC...

All function parameters have to be put in brackets even when a single value. Since 99.9% of all cases are single values, e.g., PEEK 32768, CHR$ 65, STR$ RND, etc., Spectrum BASIC is clearly superior in that it only demands brackets for calculated values, e.g., PEEK (N+3), CHR$(X*8*2).

VAL is extremely feeble in QB.It does not return the value of a string but merely the value of the first digits it finds! For example, VAL"1+2+3+4" returns only 1 because it stops at the first non-digit while VAL"(1+1)" gives 0 because it stops at the first bracket!

There is no 'PRINT AT' so it is not possible to do...

PRINT AT 3,3;"MENU";AT 6,8;"ABC" ;AT 10,4;"ETC. ETC."

You have to use...

LOCATE 3,3 : PRINT "MENU" LOCATE 6,8 : PRINT "ABC" LOCATE 10,4: PRINT "ETC. ETC."

Nor is there a PRINT apostrophe so you can't...

PRINT'''"ONE"'''"TWO"'''"THREE"

:..but have to repeat PRINT PRINT PRINT          ...over and over!

Use of the mouse is strange too! There is a separate cursor you can move rapidly to anywhere in the listing,click and the normal is placed there - a quick way to move around. However,it tries to be too clever and doesn't place the text cursor right where the mouse cursor is but jumps to a nearby keyword or space between data. In fact, I cannot work out how it decides what to do! It is annoying as it is easy to put the mouse cursor right on the spot you want to edit only to find it jumps 6 characters away! Furthermore,the word or data you are on may auto-delete when you start to type! I think this is while it is highlighted so one has to take care to cursor first and the highlight disappears.

The mouse scroll bar too makes no sense to me at all on wide screens and it seems impossible to guess where it will end up!

The brackets on the PC keyboard are one to the right of where they are on the Spectrum and SAM keyboards,DELETE is out of range many other keys are different.It is difficult because I have to keep using different computers all day!

One other thing... In most modes you cannot even PRINT text on a different coloured 'PAPER' back- ground but only on the main screen colour! Also, the border, although smaller than a Spectrum remains black!! .

There are other problems but, having said all that, ALL comp- uters have their oddities. The way the 48K listing scrolls and rolls on the Spectrum drives me potty unless I have my TOPLIST (OUTLET 17) installed!

Once one gets used to one system then anything new and different seems alien and awkward. I have outlined frustrations in QBASIC yet as one gets used to them I can assure readers that there are many exciting new features and incredible speed. If you had been having doubts about getting a PC then I can assure you that I am enjoying it tremendously.If you like programming in BASIC, I think you'll like it too.

Like you, I found that the DRAW command seemed awkward. However, a week or so later I needed to create a text routine to give different sizes and styles of text which we could use in any future OUTLET on headers,prompts etc. DRAW turned out to be perf- ect for this as any character can be redrawn to any scale, in any colour and even tilted to give italics! It can also have a border, be pattern-filled and a 3D shadowing!

Although my routine will not be finished for some time, I hope to put it in a future OUTLET PC. I think it will probably meet your needs for a text routine similar to Buttercraft's!

Now to your emulator problem. I assume this is the Lunter one? You can get a null modem cable to link your computers but if you have a serial cable on your PC and another on your +3 then a cheaper way is to get a null modem adaptor which links the two.

HOWEVER, the problem is that you need a program both at the +3 end AND on the PC to transfer the software and as I understand it there is nothing suitable at present.

I would advise you to order the new 128K version of the emulator from BG SERVICES (see OUTBOARD) and use tape transfer.

BG are planning to build a few PC tape interfaces for those who do not feel confident enough to make one up themselves. If you ask, perhaps you can place an advance order.

If you then use +3 TAPER (OUTLET 69), it will automatically save your selected +3 programs from +3 disc to tape and thence to PC (all this presupposes you have a cassette recorder!).

The Lunter emulator has really been geared up for +D disc as the 3.5" format is standard.

### From L.G. Baumann, SOUTH AFRICA

Дорогие R & B,

3 апреля 1992 года я отправил вам две программы, получение которых вы подтвердили.

Первой была «Oxo Play» (63 сектора) — программа «Крестики-нолики» с изюминкой. Ее можно было настроить на случайную игру, на игру от обороны или же на атаку компьютера с расстановкой ловушек.

Второй была «Oxo Traps» (38 секторов) — наглядное пособие, показывающее все возможные варианты «ловушек», а также содержащее игровое поле, на котором любой желающий мог расставлять нолики и крестики по своему усмотрению, чтобы планировать стратегии и смотреть на результат.

Обе программы объединяло общее меню.

Я заметил, что на мартовском диске было много свободного места — 48 свободных слотов и 431 килобайт — и я рискну предположить, что теперь, когда версия для Spectrum отделена от SAM, эти программы вполне могли бы войти в раздел «Add-enders».

Программы полностью завершены и могут быть скопированы ровно в том виде, в каком я их вам передал. Я уверен, что это добавило бы интереса к вашей подборке материалов.

Буду рад услышать ваши комментарии.

Еще раз спасибо за отличное «издание» и спасибо множеству ваших авторов. Я нахожу решение Malcolm Goodman's головоломки о переменных, опубликованное Ettrick Thomson в ноябрьском выпуске 1992 года, просто превосходным.

Пока еще не было опубликовано никаких решений для следующей головоломки — о том, как обрабатывать большие числа. Francis Miles в своей превосходной и весьма универсальной бухгалтерской программе «BOOKKEEPER», похоже, нашел решение. Есть еще один момент, который меня озадачивает, и, возможно, вы или кто-то из читателей сможете его прояснить...

Возможно, на диске есть какая-то скрытая область, о которой нам не говорят, где хранится полная карта занятости секторов, изменяющаяся при каждом сохранении и удалении? Или Plus D быстро считывает весь каталог каждый раз при выполнении Save или Erase и строит временную карту где-то в памяти? Или как-то еще?

### Brian Cavers to L.G. Baumann

По совпадению, мы поместили ваши отличные программы серии OXO в ADDENDERS в прошлом месяце еще до того, как прочитали ваше письмо! Приносим извинения за задержку, но это хороший повод напомнить читателям, что публикация присланных материалов может занять от одного-двух до многих месяцев.

Причин тому несколько: во-первых, очередь из других ожидающих программ; во-вторых, стремление соблюдать баланс различных типов программ в каждом выпуске; в-третьих, сложности при редактировании (реальные или мнимые), и еще одна проблема — поиск места под конкретные программы.

Хотя на дисковой версии OUTLET для +D места часто бывает предостаточно, многие читатели забывают, что программы должны помещаться и в другие версии журнала. Версия для Opus является критическим пределом (за исключением ADDENDERS) — около 180K, следом идет +3 с ограничением в 203K.

Еще одна проблема с вашими программами заключалась в том, что на диске их связать было легко, но как нам отредактировать их для кассетной версии?

В конце концов мы решили оставить их практически без изменений (за исключением наших строк переноса, необходимых для перехода между системами) и поместить OXO в ADDENDERS.

Оглядываясь назад, мы могли бы поместить OXO в ADDENDERS еще несколько месяцев назад, но возникло еще одно осложнение: в прошлом году Chris Oliver взял на себя подготовку программ для OUTLET, и у меня ушли месяцы на то, чтобы найти время, разобрать свои архивы и отправить ему не только накопившиеся материалы, но и сопутствующую информацию.

Еще одним неосознанным фактором могло стать то, что, хотя ваша программа OXO определенно заслуживала публикации (поскольку я посчитал ее абсолютным и исчерпывающим шедевром по данной теме), у нас до этого уже было как минимум две программы «КРЕСТИКИ-НОЛИКИ», так что, возможно, чисто подсознательно ее приоритет немного снизился.

Я столь подробно (хотя и далеко не исчерпывающе!) остановился на общей проблеме некоторых (но не всех!) причин задержки публикации присланных программ потому, что считаю важным, чтобы все читатели представляли себе, что происходит за кулисами.

Могу добавить, что хорошая очередь из программ — это очень здоровый знак, и вот когда присланные материалы начнут попадать сразу в следующий номер, тогда нам всем и стоит начать беспокоиться!

Добавлю также, что мы ведем тщательный учет всех присылаемых программ и сохраняем резервную копию каждой на отдельном диске, так что не переживайте, вас не забудут.

Сказав это, полагаю, нам не стоит слишком задирать нос, так что если кто-то ДЕЙСТВИТЕЛЬНО переживает, когда же выйдет его шедевр, непременно упомяните об этом в следующем письме — мы не против немного продвинуть материал вперед, если это возможно.

Что касается вашего вопроса о карте занятости +D — вы угадали: эта карта действительно создается по мере необходимости путем объединения карт занятости каждого отдельного файла в одну общую большую карту. Это делается с помощью простой машинной инструкции OR, о чем вы наверняка знаете, и этот процесс достаточно быстр даже для полностью заполненного диска. Я использую похожую процедуру в своем файловом копировщике CATLOADER.

Я не знаю точно, ГДЕ именно строится эта временная карта, но почти наверняка это происходит в ОЗУ +D и Disciple, так что ее можно выследить с помощью тестового диска с известными занятыми секторами и новой программы PEEK @, которую я написал и которая со временем появится в OUTLET. Конечно, на это может уйти несколько месяцев, ведь тут у нас очередь...

Brian

### Francis Miles
"Windrush"  
Rabley Heath  
Welwyn  
Herts AL6 9UF  
Tel: (0438) 813406  

Дорогие Ron и Brian,

Я заметил, что Malcolm Perry (в OUTLETTER из OUTLET 69) спрашивает о версии OCP Editor/Assembler и Toolkit для +D: полагаю, он имеет в виду «and Test Tool», поскольку OCP «Machine Code Test Tool» включен в состав Editor/Assembler, тогда как «BASIC Toolkit» — это отдельная программа.

Насколько мне известно, я являюсь единственным обладателем версии EA для DISCiPLE/+D: я получил ее от Bruce Gordon (кажется, он сделал ее сам) на самых ранних этапах существования DISCiPLE. Не думаю, что она когда-либо распространялась коммерчески.

Я активно ею пользовался, но в ней были кое-какие недостатки, и в итоге я дал себе труд дизассемблировать ее и переписать по-своему: эту версию я назвал EA2.

Затем я снова переписал ее, переведя все процедуры SAVE/LOAD/LPRINT на BASIC; эта версия EA3 теоретически работает с любой дисковой/микродрайвной системой или принтером, плюс я добавил кое-какие улучшения тут и там. (Она не работает на 128K, и я почти уверен, что не заработает на +3).

Я сам пользуюсь EA3 уже несколько лет, но так и не собрался полностью избавить ее от ошибок и поэтому не пытался продавать. Между прочим, я также написал дизассемблер, который считывает машинный код и превращает его в файл исходного текста, пригодный для редактирования в EA3.

Я провел некоторую работу над EA4, которая предназначалась для 128K и должна была использовать электронный диск (RAM-диск) для ускорения ассемблирования и, возможно, для поддержки еще больших объемов кода — EA3 может собирать до 20K машинного кода, но такое ассемблирование занимает около 20 минут. Однако я увяз в попытках сделать программу слишком уж заумной! — и забросил ее, переключившись на другие дела.

Сейчас я вернулся к EA3 и надеюсь в скором времени предложить отлаженную коммерческую версию, возможно, используя некоторые дополнительные идеи, разработанные для EA4.

Делал ли когда-нибудь OUTLET обзор различных доступных программ-ассемблеров (и, возможно, даже дизассемблеров)? Я просматривал те, что вы время от времени публиковали, но так и не возникло искушения отказаться от программы OCP, которой в разных вариациях я пользуюсь уже почти десять лет.

Теперь о некоторых ошибках в ROM Index...

Я занимался процедурами магнитофонных SAVE/LOAD и обнаружил довольно серьезную ошибку в расчетах таймингов в моем ROM Index; в основном под заголовками LD EDGE 1 и LD EDGE 2, но последствия затрагивают и другие статьи, где обсуждаются временные характеристики работы с лентой.

Отчасти это произошло из-за опечатки в одном из моих справочников! Там указано время выполнения IN A,(nn) как 11 тактов, тогда как на самом деле их всего 10. Таким образом, цикл выборки в LD EDGE 1 занимает 58 тактов, а не 59 (Logan и O'Hara были правы), и большинство ошибок проистекает именно отсюда. ### Brian Cavers — Chris Benyon

Большое спасибо за информацию о вашем PC. Вы не указали, какой у вас процессор — 286, 386 или 486, но вряд ли меньше 286-го. Мне начинает казаться, что на машинах слабее 286 уже почти никто не сидит.

Я согласен, что переходить на чужой BASIC после спектрумовского — это ОЧЕНЬ мучительно. Я уже проходил через это на ST и в итоге бросил всё в полном отвращении. Поэтому я заранее ожидал сложностей, когда садился за QUICK BASIC на PC. Впрочем, прошлый опыт «перезакалил» меня, так что хоть раздражение и присутствует, мне уже не так тяжело!

Вот что в QUICK BASIC буквально выводит меня из себя:

Все параметры функций приходится брать в скобки, даже когда это одиночное значение. А поскольку в 99.9% случаев речь идет именно об одиночных значениях — например, `PEEK 32768`, `CHR$ 65`, `STR$ RND` и т.д., Spectrum BASIC явно превосходит его, требуя скобок только для вычисляемых выражений вроде `PEEK (N+3)`, `CHR$(X*8*2)`.

Функция VAL в QB невероятно убога. Она возвращает не числовое значение строки, а лишь значение первых попавшихся цифр! Например, `VAL"1+2+3+4"` вернет всего лишь 1, потому что споткнется на первом же нецифровом символе, а `VAL"(1+1)"` выдаст 0, срезавшись на первой же скобке!

Там нет `PRINT AT`, поэтому нельзя написать:

```text
PRINT AT 3,3;"MENU";AT 6,8;"ABC";AT 10,4;"ETC. ETC."
```

Приходится городить:

```text
LOCATE 3,3 : PRINT "MENU"
LOCATE 6,8 : PRINT "ABC"
LOCATE 10,4: PRINT "ETC. ETC."
```

Нет и апострофа в PRINT, так что нельзя сделать:

```text
PRINT'''"ONE"'''"TWO"'''"THREE"
```

...а приходится снова и снова повторять:

```text
PRINT
PRINT
PRINT
```

Работа с мышью — тоже сплошные странности! Есть отдельный курсор, который можно быстро переместить в любое место листинга: щелкаешь — и туда встает обычный текстовый курсор. Вроде бы быстрый способ перемещения. Однако редактор пытается казаться слишком умным и ставит курсор не туда, где был курсор мыши, а перескакивает на ближайшее ключевое слово или пробел между данными. Я вообще не могу понять, какой логикой он руководствуется! Это ужасно раздражает: наводишь курсор точно на то место, которое хочешь отредактировать, а он берет и скачет символов на 6 в сторону! Кроме того, слово или данные, на которых вы оказались, могут автоматически удалиться, когда вы начнете печатать! Кажется, это происходит, если текст выделен, так что приходится сначала нажимать клавишу со стрелкой, чтобы снять выделение.

Полоса прокрутки для мыши на широких экранах для меня тоже лишена всякого смысла — совершенно невозможно угадать, куда она в итоге улетит!

Скобки на клавиатуре PC сдвинуты на одну клавишу вправо по сравнению с клавиатурами Spectrum и SAM, DELETE находится далеко, многие другие клавиши тоже расположены иначе. Мне тяжело привыкнуть, потому что приходится весь день прыгать с одного компьютера на другой!

И еще... В большинстве режимов вы даже не можете напечатать текст на фоне другого цвета ('PAPER') — только на цвете основного экрана! А бордюр, хоть он и меньше спектрумовского, все равно остается черным!!

Есть и другие проблемы, но, если уж на то пошло, свои странности найдутся у ЛЮБОГО компьютера. То, как прокручивается листинг в 48K на Спектруме, доводит меня до белого каления, если не установлена моя TOPLIST (OUTLET 17)!

Когда привыкаешь к одной системе, все новое и непривычное кажется чуждым и неудобным. Я перечислил раздражающие моменты в QBASIC, но могу заверить читателей: стоит к ним притерпеться, как открываешь массу восхитительных новых возможностей и невероятную скорость работы. Если вы сомневались, стоит ли покупать PC, то уверяю вас: я получаю от него колоссальное удовольствие. Если вам нравится программировать на BASIC, думаю, понравится и он.

Как и вам, команда DRAW сначала показалась мне неудобной. Однако примерно неделю спустя мне понадобилось создать текстовую подпрограмму для отрисовки надписей разных размеров и стилей, которую мы могли бы использовать в будущих номерах OUTLET для заголовков, подсказок и т.д. Команда DRAW подошла для этого идеально: любой символ можно перерисовать в любом масштабе, любым цветом и даже наклонить, сделав курсивом! Можно добавить контур, узорную заливку и объемную тень!

Хотя моя подпрограмма будет готова еще нескоро, я надеюсь включить ее в будущий выпуск OUTLET PC. Думаю, она вполне покроет ваши запросы по части работы с текстом, как это было в софте от Buttercraft!

Теперь насчет вашей проблемы с эмулятором. Полагаю, речь идет об эмуляторе Lunter? Компьютеры можно соединить нуль-модемным кабелем, но если у вас уже есть последовательный кабель для PC и еще один для +3, дешевле будет купить нуль-модемный переходник, который свяжет их вместе.

ОДНАКО проблема в том, что вам понадобится программа как на стороне +3, ТАК И на PC для передачи файлов, а насколько мне известно, ничего подходящего сейчас нет.

Затем, если воспользоваться программой +3 TAPER (OUTLET 69), она автоматически перепишет выбранные вами программы с дискет +3 на кассету, а оттуда — уже на PC (все это, конечно, при условии, что у вас есть магнитофон!).

Эмулятор Lunter на самом деле «заточен» под дисководы +D, поскольку формат 3.5" там стандартный.
